author: high
claim: Solved directly: the full Vandermonde determinant identity for every positive integer n and all real x_1,...,x_n.
evidence: Proof by induction on n. For n=1 the determinant is det(1)=1 and the product over the empty set of pairs is 1. Assume the identity for n-1. Denote the columns of the n by n matrix by C_1,...,C_n. For k=n,n-1,...,2, replace C_k with C_k-x_1C_{k-1}. These operations preserve the determinant, and the descending order ensures C_{k-1} is unmodified when used. The transformed first row is (1,0,...,0), while for i>=2 and k>=2 the transformed entry is (x_i-x_1)x_i^{k-2}. Expanding along the first row and factoring x_i-x_1 from each remaining row gives D_n=\prod_{i=2}^n(x_i-x_1)D_{n-1}(x_2,...,x_n). The induction hypothesis makes the latter determinant \prod_{2<=i<j<=n}(x_j-x_i). Multiplication gives \prod_{1<=i<j<=n}(x_j-x_i), since the factors with i=1 are exactly \prod_{j=2}^n(x_j-x_1). No distinctness assumption is used.
